title: Denial Codes and Appeal Levels — Wound Care Supply Program
content:
# Denial codes and appeal levels — Wound Care Supply Program

Denial management grid for claim denials on the Wound Care Supply Program. A denial is worked by its denial code, and the code alone decides the route; the Wound Care Self-Pay Program has no denials or appeals.

## Grid by denial code

| Code | Meaning | Route |
|---|---|---|
| CO-16 | claim lacks information | unprocessable and never appealed; cured only by a corrected claim transmitted no later than the tier's corrected-claim window, in calendar days, after the denial's posting date |
| CO-50 | not medically necessary | appealable |
| CO-151 | frequency or quantity not supported | appealable only when a medical record supporting the quantity, dated on or before the date of service, is on file; otherwise not appealed and handled as a non-covered amount under the advance notice of financial liability rules |
| CO-197 | authorization absent | appealable only when an authorization grant valid on the date of service is on file; otherwise not appealed and handled as a non-covered amount under the advance notice of financial liability rules |
| CO-29 | timely filing expired | never appealed and never billed to the customer; Larkfield writes it off with a billing correction adjustment |
| PR-204 | not covered under the plan | becomes the customer's responsibility only under the advance notice of financial liability rules; otherwise Larkfield absorbs it |

## Appeal levels

- **First level.** A first-level appeal may be filed no later than the tier's first-level appeal window, in calendar days, after the posting date of the denial it appeals, counted in calendar days from that posting date with the last day allowed.
- **Upheld decision.** An appeal decision that upholds the denial posts as a new denial whose original posting is the appeal filing.
- **Second level.** A second-level appeal may be filed only against such an upheld first-level decision, no later than the tier's second-level appeal window, in calendar days, after its posting date. Where the second-level window is 0 there is no customer-filed second level on the tier, and on the Wound Care Medicare Advantage Program the plan forwards an upheld denial to the independent review entity itself.
- **One per level.** One appeal is filed per level per denial; a denial already appealed at a level is not appealed again at that level.

## First-level window (hypothetical figures)

Denial posted 2026-01-12 on a tier with a 65-day first-level window: an appeal filed on 2026-03-18 is within the window (the last day is allowed); an appeal filed on 2026-03-19 is not.

## Points of judgement

- *A CO-197 denial for a dressing shipped on a date that an authorization grant on file covered.* The denial is appealable at the first level within the window.
- *A CO-16 denial.* It is not appealed; only a corrected claim within the corrected-claim window cures it.
- *A denial already appealed at the first level.* No second first-level appeal is filed on it.
